title: Brass band tempos and the best bands from LaPlace
summary: Braud explains brass bands used six-eighth and two-four time on the street, and praises the Dejan and Claiborne Williams brass bands, who read and improvised.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: They have what they call six-eighth time. They have what they call to play some in two full time. See what I mean? Well, who would use those? Well, brass bands, like a minister band, they use six-eighth time for the street. You understand? And some tunes, they used two full times. And some tunes, yeah, two full times, like Sally Trombone, that was a great street number, because there was plenty of trombone in there. You remember that? There had plenty of trombone in there. Yeah. They have two trombones in the front, and the two was in the back. So that was very exciting. The guy had on the long coats, you remember? Boy, I don't know if that's before your time, you know, we wouldn't remember. Yeah. You've seen the pictures, the guy with the high hat on. Well, that was very exciting. The music was good. You could pick up good brass bands today, at that time. The best brass band coming, Yorling, was a fellow by the name of Dejan from Laplace, and Clayman Williams. That's the best brass band ever hit them streets out there buying nobody. Yeah, Dejan. Is that one if he's related to Harold Dejan that plays Alto here? I don't know, but Dejan, I'm speaking about, is from Laplace. Must be the same. Oh, there's some good musicians coming from Laplace. Yeah, must be the same. In reserve. Dejan brand read everything they play, but they could improvise. That's where Hall came from. Hall's father was a clown that played.
